clue.text: You shouldn't have holiday sex with wretched Keir to please yourself (4,2,2,5,2)

indicators.note: a wretched thing is in a sorry state, and letters in a sorry state have fallen out of the order they were given

blocks.note: what you say when handed a present, in its shortest form: ta, meaning thanks
the Labour leader's first name and the little word after it, six letters between them
leave is the time off work a soldier or an employee is granted
it has been a coy word for sex since the days of the It girl

explanation.walkthrough: Both 'ta' and 'you shouldn't have' are what you say when someone hands you a present, which is the joke holding the front of the clue up.
explanation.definitionFit: please yourself -> TAKE IT OR LEAVE IT: both are the same dismissive shrug, an offer put on the table with the choice handed entirely to you.

clue.text: Labour introducing shifting scale that makes sparks fly (5,4)

indicators.note: to introduce something is to bring it in, so the new letters arrive inside the word already there
what shifts will not stay put, so the letters move off the positions the clue prints them in

blocks.note: labour is toil, the plain word for hard graft
the five letters of the word, shifted into a new order

explanation.walkthrough: Labour with a capital L is the party and a scale is a fish's or a musician's; the wordplay wants hard work and a measuring device instead.
explanation.definitionFit: that makes sparks fly -> TESLA COIL: Tesla's resonant transformer throws visible high-voltage arcs, so the phrase names the machine by the display it is built for.

clue.text: Orderly looked after nurses close to sanatorium (5)

indicators.note: to nurse a patient is to hold them in your care, so this word wraps itself round what follows
the close of a word is where it finishes, and only that final letter is wanted

blocks.note: to look after a thing is to keep it
the letter the word finishes on

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a hospital ward, where an orderly is a member of staff. The definition wants the adjective, a word almost nobody uses except with un- in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Orderly -> KEMPT: kempt describes hair or a person combed and tidy, a sense that survives mainly in its negative and in crosswords.

clue.text: Third off price for ham? (5)

indicators.note: count three letters into the word beside it and take that one away with you; in a five-letter word it is the one at dead centre

blocks.note: the third of its five letters, and the middle one

explanation.walkthrough: Radio hams spell letters out with the international alphabet, so one letter and a whole word are the same thing said two ways. The pork and the discount are pure surface.
explanation.definitionFit: for ham? -> INDIA: an amateur radio operator reads the letter I aloud as India, the NATO alphabet word, so the answer is a single letter spoken.

clue.text: One beastly Conservative's unguarded kiss (4)

indicators.note: a guard stands at the edge, so a word left unguarded loses the letter posted at each of its ends

blocks.note: a Conservative is a TORY, and with its 's that is five letters; the two on sentry duty at either end walk off
the X scribbled at the foot of a letter

explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s looks like possession and is really the fifth letter of the fodder, which is what makes the sentries land where they do.
explanation.definitionFit: One beastly -> ORYX: 'beastly' points at the animal kingdom and 'one' at a single member of it, and this member is a straight-horned desert antelope.

clue.text: Key expert's cant in hearing (5)

indicators.note: what is taken in hearing is judged by ear alone, so the spelling you write down need not be the spelling you were given

blocks.note: to cant is to tilt, and a ship that tilts is said to list; that is the word being spoken

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a locksmith or a piano tuner talking jargon. 'Cant' also means insincere talk, which is the sense the clue wants you to hear first.
explanation.definitionFit: Key expert -> LISZT: the Hungarian virtuoso was the supreme master of the piano keyboard, so the definition names him by the black and white keys.

clue.text: TV show possibly exposed sporting star as one who gets high (9)

indicators.note: this warns that what follows is only one possible member of the class, not the class itself
something exposed has had its covering taken off, and a word's covering is the letter at each end
to sport a hat or a tan is to wear it, so whatever is sported is worn on the outside of the other piece

blocks.note: the A-list is where the famous names sit, so an A-lister is a star
a SERIAL is one kind of TV show, with the letter at each end taken off

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sporting star' reads as an athlete and wants a celebrity, and 'one who gets high' points at a trapeze rather than a habit.
explanation.definitionFit: one who gets high -> AERIALIST: an aerialist performs on the trapeze or the high wire, so getting high is literally the job description.

clue.text: Europeans disturbed by news on international lack of interest (5)

indicators.note: what disturbs you gets inside you, so this piece lands in the middle of the one before it
in a down entry one thing sits on another by being written above it, so what follows goes underneath

blocks.note: the union the Europeans built, in its two-letter form
N is the abbreviation for new, and a doubled letter is how crosswords write its plural
I is the standard short form of international, as on a fixture list

explanation.walkthrough: Being disturbed by news is what happens to a reader and what happens to the letters, which is the whole of the surface's trick.
explanation.definitionFit: lack of interest -> ENNUI: the French loan word for a listless boredom in which nothing seems worth attending to, stronger than ordinary idleness.

clue.text: Cover of The Modern Age sampling Queen track (5)

indicators.note: a cover is what goes round the outside, so the letters wanted are the ones at either edge
sampling a record drops a piece of one track into the middle of another, and these letters do the same

blocks.note: the letters at the two edges of the word, its covers
AD, anno domini, is the era we are still counting in
R for Regina, the Latin the monarch signs with

explanation.walkthrough: The italics make The Modern Age one Strokes title, and the wordplay refuses to read it that way: the first word and the other two are handled separately.
explanation.definitionFit: track -> TREAD: the pattern moulded into a tyre is its tread, and the marks it leaves are tracks, so the two words meet on the road.

clue.text: One quits newspapers possibly drowning in sauce sooner or later (7)

indicators.note: someone who quits walks out and does not come back, and the letter beside it goes the same way
a warning that the word before it names only one possible member of a wider class
what drowns goes under the surface of the liquid, so this piece ends up inside the other

blocks.note: soy is the sauce in the little bottle on the table
newspapers are one branch of the media
the Roman numeral for one, and the letter that walks out

explanation.walkthrough: The 'one' quitting is a numeral rather than a resigning journalist, and 'possibly' is the flag that newspapers stand for something broader.
explanation.definitionFit: sooner or later -> SOMEDAY: both phrases promise a future occasion while refusing to name it, which is what makes them interchangeable.

clue.text: To choke, losing heart in Wimbledon, is hard to explain (7)

indicators.note: what you lose you no longer have, so those letters do not reach the answer
the heart of a word is the letter at its exact centre, which only an odd-numbered word has

blocks.note: to choke someone is to STRANGLE them, and this is that verb with one letter pulled out
nine letters, so the fifth stands at the dead centre

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a player bottling it on Centre Court, and Wimbledon is in the clue to be counted rather than played.
explanation.definitionFit: hard to explain -> STRANGE: what is strange resists explanation because it matches no pattern you already hold, which is why the two phrases swap.

clue.text: Vauxhall car approaching yard is off course (6)

indicators.note: what approaches comes right up against the thing it nears, so these letters sit immediately in front

blocks.note: the Astra is Vauxhall's long-running family hatchback
Y is the abbreviation for a yard on a ruler

explanation.walkthrough: Vauxhall is a car marque, a London district and a football ground; only the badge on the bonnet is wanted here.
explanation.definitionFit: off course -> ASTRAY: a ship off course has wandered from the route it meant to take, and going astray is that same straying, on land or in morals.

clue.text: Made firm second date arranged with bombshell (8)

indicators.note: an arrangement is somebody's chosen order, so the letters are free to be set out afresh

blocks.note: s is the second on a stopwatch
the four letters of the word, set out in a new order
an IED is an improvised explosive device, a home-made bomb

explanation.walkthrough: A bombshell is a blonde on the surface and a piece of ordnance in the wordplay, and 'second date' is a romance rather than an abbreviation plus fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Made firm -> STEADIED: to steady a thing is to stop it wobbling, and the past tense reports that job already done.

clue.text: American woman who won five Grand Slam titles (4)

definitions.text: who won five Grand Slam titles

blocks.note: A is the standard abbreviation for American
the pronoun you use of a woman

explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is two small pieces, so the whole clue rests on one false statement: it calls the player a woman, and the player was not one.
explanation.definitionFit: who won five Grand Slam titles -> ASHE: Arthur Ashe took three singles majors and two more in doubles, five in all, at the height of the 1970s.

clue.text: Republicans originally redacted models' faces (7)

indicators.note: the original letter is the one the word starts with, and that is the one being pointed at
a redacted word has had a part blacked out, and what is blacked out never reaches the answer

blocks.note: the Republicans are the Grand Old Party, the GOP, docked of the letter it opens with
a model poses for the camera

explanation.walkthrough: GOP for the American Republicans is the piece to bank here, and 'faces' is the definition working hard to look like a noun about cheekbones.
explanation.definitionFit: faces -> OPPOSES: to face something is to stand against it and confront it, the same third-person verb the answer supplies.

clue.text: Character from The Odyssey that’s acidic? (3)

blocks.note: how acid a liquid is gets measured on the pH scale
Roman one: a reading of 1 on that scale is about as acid as liquids get

explanation.walkthrough: Homer wrote in Greek, so a character from his poem is a letter of that alphabet rather than a hero. The scale runs 0 to 14, and the numeral is written the Roman way.
explanation.definitionFit: Character from The Odyssey -> PHI: the poem is Greek, so its characters in the typographic sense are the letters of the Greek alphabet, of which this is one.

clue.text: Four times Sugar wasted capital in Baden-Württemberg (9)

indicators.note: something laid waste is left in ruins, and letters in ruins keep none of their original order

blocks.note: t is the scientist's symbol for time, and four of them are asked for
the whole word goes into the mix

explanation.walkthrough: The Sugar of the surface is Alan, and 'four times' looks like a frequency until you notice that time has a one-letter symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: capital in Baden-Württemberg -> STUTTGART: the seat of government of that German state, home to Mercedes and Porsche, named here by its region rather than its country.

clue.text: Extremely cool remix of Strokes' Last Nite for those that pay (7)

indicators.note: at the extremes means at the two ends, so you keep the outermost letter on each side and drop everything between
a remix builds a new track out of the same material, which is what happens to these letters
the last of a word is the letter it finishes on, and that single letter joins the material

blocks.note: the letters at either edge of the word, with the middle discarded
the last letter of the band's name, and nothing else of it
the song title's four letters, ready to be rebuilt

explanation.walkthrough: The Strokes released Last Nite in 2001, and the apostrophe does double duty: possession on the surface, and a pointer to one letter in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: those that pay -> CLIENTS: a client is someone who buys a professional's time, so the phrase names them by the fee rather than the service.

clue.text: Meloni's opener: "Trump's intelligence? Zero!" (4)

blocks.note: the Central Intelligence Agency answers to the American president
a nought is written as a round O

explanation.walkthrough: Giorgia Meloni is Italy's prime minister, so the word she opens with is Italian, and the surface's joke about presidential intelligence is doing the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Meloni's opener -> CIAO: the Italian greeting an Italian speaker leads with, and the same word again on parting.

clue.text: Collar's missing a zip (3)

indicators.note: the letter that goes is named right there in the clue: a single A leaves the word beside it

blocks.note: to collar a suspect is to NAIL them, and this is that word one letter lighter

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a jacket with a broken fastening; the definition is the American slang for nothing, and 'collar' has to be read as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: zip -> NIL: zip is slang for nothing at all, and this is the word for nothing that a scoreboard uses, so both name zero.

clue.text: Insignificant banker's unacceptable service on the back of jet (9)

indicators.note: riding on the back of a thing means coming along behind it, so these letters follow rather than lead

blocks.note: a jet of water is a stream of it
a serve that clips the net is a let and will not be accepted, so it is taken again

explanation.walkthrough: Banker for river is one of the oldest crossword conventions, on the grounds that a river is the thing with banks; the surface's bonus and bank job are decoys.
explanation.definitionFit: Insignificant banker -> STREAMLET: the banker is a watercourse, and the -let ending shrinks it to something too small to matter.

clue.text: The French certain to embrace current convenient opportunity (7)

indicators.note: an embrace closes arms round whoever is held, so the letters go one on each side of what follows

blocks.note: the definite article as the French write it
someone certain of a thing is sure of it
I is the physicist's symbol for electric current

explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' is the electrical kind, not the present-day kind, and the French article is a crossword staple worth banking alongside LA and LES.
explanation.definitionFit: convenient opportunity -> LEISURE: at your leisure means whenever it suits you, so the noun names time free to be used as you choose.

clue.text: Tips from angry sub: "Trying your luck annoys readers wanting columns" (7)

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its topmost point, so one letter comes off the front of each word named

blocks.clueFragment: angry sub: "Trying your luck annoys readers
blocks.note: the seven words each hand over the letter they begin with, in the order they are printed

explanation.walkthrough: A sub-editor's columns are inches of newsprint and an architect's are pillars, which is the whole of the joke; the quoted grumble is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: wanting columns -> ASTYLAR: the architect's word for a front built without pillars, from the Greek stylos, a column, with the negative a- in front.

clue.text: United’s lead cut by player’s mistake ... (8)

indicators.note: something that cuts into a thing lands in the middle of it, splitting what it enters

blocks.note: the lead you walk a dog on is a tether
OG is how a scoreline records an own goal

explanation.walkthrough: The capital U makes it a football club and the ellipsis runs the sentence on into 25 across, so nothing in the surface admits it is a clue about dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: United -> TOGETHER: to stand united is to stand as one, which is what doing anything together means; the club name is the misdirection.

clue.text: Half-hearted old Tory enforcer upset region in dispute (5)

indicators.note: a word with twin letters at its heart can be halved there, and only one of the pair survives
something upset has been tipped over, so the letters are read in the opposite order

blocks.note: Norman TEBBIT was the Conservatives' chairman and hard man, here with one of the twins at his centre gone

explanation.walkthrough: Tebbit was Margaret Thatcher's party chairman, the 'on yer bike' man; the setter likes the name for the pair of letters sitting at its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: region in dispute -> TIBET: the Himalayan territory China governs and a government-in-exile claims, so the definition names it by that unresolved status.

clue.text: Eagle going around after golf class (5)

indicators.note: a thing going around comes back the way it went, so its letters run in the opposite order
what comes after follows on behind, which in a down entry means further down the column

blocks.note: golf is how the radio alphabet says G
an ERNE is a sea eagle, its four letters turned about

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a round of golf, where an eagle is two under par; the wordplay wants the bird, and the erne is the crossword's standard one.
explanation.definitionFit: class -> GENRE: a genre is a class of books, films or music grouped by shared form, so one noun of category stands for the other.

clue.text: Space kept by priest for fragrant resin (5)

indicators.note: whatever is kept by someone is held within their keeping, so this piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: Eli is the Old Testament priest who brought up Samuel
an em is the printer's space, as wide as the letter M is cast

explanation.walkthrough: Two conventions worth banking: the biblical three-letter priest, and the typesetter's em, which turns up whenever a clue mentions space or width.
explanation.definitionFit: fragrant resin -> ELEMI: elemi is the soft aromatic gum tapped from canarium trees in the Philippines and used in varnishes and incense.

clue.text: ... short cross Rayan Aït-Nouri initially returned back to Donnarumma for City (6)

indicators.note: cut short means stopped before the end, so the last letter never gets written
what happens initially happens at the very start, so only the opening letter of each name is taken
a ball returned comes straight back the way it came, and so do these letters
the back of a name is the letter it ends on, and that is all that is wanted from it

blocks.note: an ANKH is the looped Egyptian cross, one letter shorter here
the initials of the defender's two names, read the other way round
the letter the goalkeeper's name ends on

explanation.walkthrough: The dots carry the sentence on from 22 across, and the surface is football commentary: both players named turn out for the other City in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: City -> ANKARA: Turkey's capital, chosen over Istanbul in 1923, so the bare word points at one city by example rather than defining the class.

clue.text: New York city cops heading to apprehend animal (5)

indicators.note: to cop something is to catch and keep it, so this piece is taken inside
the heading of a word is the letter at its top, and only that one is taken

blocks.note: the state's two-letter postal abbreviation
LA is the shorthand for Los Angeles
the letter this word starts with

explanation.walkthrough: 'New York city cops' reads as one police force and splits into two separate abbreviations, while 'cops' turns from a noun into the verb that does the enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: animal -> NYALA: definition by example, since the nyala is one particular spiral-horned antelope of southern Africa rather than the class of animals.

clue.text: Gay, maybe rampant and single! (5)

indicators.note: a flag that the word before it is only one possible bearer of the name, not the name's meaning
a heraldic beast rampant is reared up on its hind legs, so the letters stand up the other way

blocks.note: the B-29 that carried the Hiroshima bomb was the Enola Gay, named for the pilot's mother

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark is there to keep you reading 'gay' as an adjective; the wordplay wants the surname, and the first name that famously goes in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: single -> ALONE: single here means unaccompanied rather than unmarried, the sense of a person with nobody else present.

clue.text: Huxley's soporific book on revolution (4)

indicators.note: a revolution turns a thing full circle, so what was written one way comes out the other

blocks.note: AMOS is one of the twelve minor prophets and a book of the Old Testament in its own right

explanation.walkthrough: Short books of the Bible are worth learning as spare letters, and 'revolution' keeps the surface political while doing something purely mechanical.
explanation.definitionFit: Huxley's soporific -> SOMA: in Brave New World soma is the state-issued pill that dulls every citizen into contentment, a drug Huxley invented and named.

clue.text: Who's licensed to kill twisted, barely legal kink? (7)

blocks.note: the licence to kill belongs to 007, the agent Ian Fleming named
surface only: it colours the sentence and hands over no letters
being of age is what makes a thing legal, and barely of age is only just that

explanation.walkthrough: Bond has held his licence since 1953, and 'barely legal' is the surface leering at the age of consent while quietly naming a three-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: kink -> BONDAGE: kink is the everyday word for an unusual sexual taste, and being tied up is the best known of them.

clue.text: List of elite US students said to be doing well (2,1,4)

indicators.note: what is said is heard rather than read, so the letters you write need only match the sound

blocks.note: American schools post an honor roll of their best students, and an English mouth drops the aitch and runs the words together

explanation.walkthrough: The American spelling matters: an honour roll would not sound the same. Said aloud without the aitch, the words re-divide into a different phrase entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: doing well -> ON A ROLL: the idiom for a run of success, borrowed from a gambler whose dice keep coming good.

clue.text: Professional representative could be awful charlatan getting cut repeatedly: first 12.5% of earnings (10,5)

indicators.note: what is awful is in a dreadful state, and letters in a dreadful state keep none of their order
one cut takes the last letter off, and repeating it takes the next one too
an eighth of a word eight letters long is one letter, and it is the one at the front

blocks.note: all nine letters go into the mix
the seven-letter word loses its final letter, then loses the next one as well
eight letters, so an eighth of them is the first letter and no more

explanation.walkthrough: The percentage is a letter count in disguise, and the charlatan taking repeated cuts of someone's earnings is the surface's joke about commission.
explanation.definitionFit: Professional representative -> THEATRICAL AGENT: the agent who finds actors their work and takes a percentage, so the phrase names the trade by what it does.
